answered.sql: SELECT destination_name FROM Destinations WHERE id IN (SELECT destination_id FROM Bookings WHERE travel_agency_id IN (SELECT id FROM Travel_Agencies)) GROUP BY destination_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT travel_agency_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Travel_Agencies)

candidates.meaning: Retrieve the destination names associated with each travel agency.
candidates.sql: SELECT ta.name, d.destination_name FROM Travel_Agencies ta JOIN Travel_Agencies_Destinations tad ON ta.id = tad.travel_agency_id JOIN Destinations d ON tad.destination_id = d.id

candidates.meaning: List the destination names for each travel agency based on the bookings.
candidates.sql: SELECT T3.destination_name, T2.name FROM Bookings AS T1 JOIN Travel_Agencies AS T2 ON T1.travel_agency_id = T2.id JOIN Destinations AS T3 ON T1.destination_id = T3.id GROUP BY T2.name, T3.destination_name

candidates.meaning: List the destination names for each travel agency based on the direct association in the Travel_Agencies_Destinations table.
candidates.sql: SELECT T3.destination_name, T2.name FROM Travel_Agencies_Destinations AS T1 JOIN Travel_Agencies AS T2 ON T1.travel_agency_id = T2.id JOIN Destinations AS T3 ON T1.destination_id = T3.id

candidates.meaning: List the destination names for each travel agency, considering both bookings and direct associations.
candidates.sql: SELECT destination_name, name FROM (SELECT T3.destination_name, T2.name FROM Bookings AS T1 JOIN Travel_Agencies AS T2 ON T1.travel_agency_id = T2.id JOIN Destinations AS T3 ON T1.destination_id = T3.id UNION SELECT T3.destination_name, T2.name FROM Travel_Agencies_Destinations AS T1 JOIN Travel_Agencies AS T2 ON T1.travel_agency_id = T2.id JOIN Destinations AS T3 ON T1.destination_id = T3.id) GROUP BY name, destination_name
